_comment_gates: prompt/image/mesh = stop for your approval after that pipeline stage. vision = render-vision gate, one of off | focused | full: after an action the assistant renders the scene and looks at it before claiming anything visual. focused (default) covers animation, rig/mesh binding, brush placement and spawns; full adds every other look-changing step including raw bpy. Each check costs one extra vision call.
_comment_seats_vision: The model that LOOKS at renders (inspect_render + the render-vision gate). It is a judge, not an orchestrator: it is the only thing that can contradict a 'fixed' claim, so it gets its own seat. Remove this seat and it falls back to the orchestrator's model - which means changing the orchestrator would silently change the judge too. Keep them separate on purpose.
_comment_endpoints: comfyui = the ComfyUI running your image and mesh workflows. 8188 is ComfyUI's own default port; change it if you started ComfyUI with --port. local = an optional OpenAI-compatible local model server (e.g. LM Studio) for the metaprompter.
_comment_hyMotion: Text->Motion, optional. api = the ComfyUI that has ComfyUI-HY-Motion1 in custom_nodes and the weights under models/HY-Motion/. That can be the same ComfyUI as endpoints.comfyui (then leave both alike) or a separate one; what matters is that the nodes are installed there, not which port it uses. Point it at another machine (e.g. http://gpu-box.local:8188) if generation runs on a separate GPU box. template = a Mixamo REST-POSE (T-pose) FBX, relative to that ComfyUI's folder; create it with scripts/hy-motion/make_tpose_char.py.
_comment_voice: Voice AND SFX tabs, optional. api = a CrispASR speech server (start it with: crispasr --server --host 0.0.0.0 --port 8090 -m tada --voice-dir <folder of .gguf voice packs>). Leave empty to hide those tabs' functions. It may run on another machine - point it there (e.g. http://gpu-box.local:8090); generation belongs where the GPU is. ffmpeg = path to an ffmpeg binary; the voice EFFECTS and every SFX edit/bench render need it; leave empty to auto-detect the one bundled with imageio-ffmpeg, and if that finds nothing the effects fail with a clear error. A voice pack is baked once with `crispasr --make-ref` from a reference recording - reference quality is output quality, and the pack also freezes the delivery, so record calm and clean unless you want that colour in every line.
_comment_feedback: Optional. Set endpointUrl to a URL that accepts a JSON POST and the in-app Feedback form posts there; leave empty and the form stays hidden.
_comment_preflight: What `node preflight.js` compares the ComfyUI environment against. Drift is reported as a warning, not an error - set these to whatever your working install reports.
_comment_apps: blender = full path to your Blender executable, used only so Phoenix can launch it for you; optional. Windows: C:\\Program Files\\Blender Foundation\\Blender 5.1\\blender.exe - macOS: /Applications/Blender.app/Contents/MacOS/Blender - Linux: /usr/bin/blender. blenderIpcDir (not listed above, optional) = the folder Phoenix and the Blender addon exchange commands through. WARNING: setting it here only moves the PHOENIX side - the addon reads the PHOENIX_BLENDER_IPC_DIR environment variable and nothing else, so unless you ALSO start Blender with that variable set to the same path, every Blender call will time out. Leave it unset unless you know you need it. comfyOutput = the folder ComfyUI writes generated files into. Left empty, Phoenix looks in ~/Documents/ComfyUI/output, which is where ComfyUI-Desktop puts them - a portable or git install writes somewhere else, so SET THIS to <your ComfyUI folder>/output or the mesh stage will fail to collect a mesh that generated fine.
_comment_unreal: The Unreal bridge (place brushes / spawn characters into a running editor, pull assets back to Blender, screenshot the viewport) - Phoenix NEVER starts Unreal, you keep the editor open. unrealEngine = folder of your Unreal install, e.g. C:\\Program Files\\Epic Games\\UE_5.8; optional, left empty Phoenix takes the newest UE_* it can find. python = a real Python 3 the bridge helper runs; leave empty to use `python` from PATH, but on Windows avoid the Microsoft-Store stub (it exits instantly and every Unreal action fails). In the editor: enable the Python Editor Script Plugin and tick Project Settings -> Python -> Enable Remote Execution.
